It's not a "law." It's a scale. Kinsey's research was done in the 50's when there was basically no information about human sexual orientation. His research was one of the impetuses to remove homosexuality from the DSM (a volume of defined medical maladies used by doctors worldwide).

By conducting anonymous surveys, he found that homosexual characteristics were more widespread than previously thought and that sexual orientation was not fully binary. He found there was a scale of orientation based on the responses to his surveys. He also found the vast majority of people describing homosexual characteristics had no other mental illnesses. He didn't "promote" anything but a more accurate understanding of human sexuality.

How can one "refute" hard data? Kinsey saw that a significant percentage of respondents described behavior that was considered homosexual. These were anonymous surveys, so there was no reason for people to lie. He used mathematics to conclude that more people in the general population were homosexual than previously thought. It's not as if he started with an absurd proposition such as "There are no absolute truths" and ran with it.

The "born this way" concept was being studied before Lady Gaga was even born. As homosexuality became less taboo to discuss, more people described being born gay. I read an article many years ago in which a group of scientists searched for examples of homosexuality among animals. They wanted to answer the question of whether homosexuality was a choice or based in biology, thinking that if animals were gay it must be biological. They ended up finding examples of such behavior that fit every criteria for being a truly homosexual relationship. There was a pair of male geese that had been in a pair-bonded relationship for years while viable breeding females surrounded them.

Homosexuality may not be genetic per se, but it is definitely rooted in biology. Gay people don't choose to be gay; they really are born like that. All Kinsey did was help promote a better understanding of gay people.
